# Vendored crates

Permissively licensed crates we carry small patches for. Each directory keeps the upstream
licence files unchanged. Every patch is marked `PdfCraft patch:` in the source, is covered by a
PdfCraft test, and should be proposed upstream. Remove the vendored copy once upstream releases
the fix. Vendoring copyleft code is never allowed (plan/adr/0001).

| Crate | Version | Licence | Patches | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hayro-interpret | 0.7.0 | Apache-2.0 OR MIT | (1) select `/AP /N` appearance states via `/AS` (checkboxes, radios, stateful icons) and honour the NoView flag; (2) Type3 Unicode fallback to `/Encoding` glyph names, then printable ASCII; (3) `Type3Glyph::advance_width`; (4) `InterpreterSettings::ocg_overrides` for viewer layer toggles; (5) soft masks whose group lacks `/CS` were dropped (Chrome gradient text); (6) paint nesting cap `MAX_PAINT_NESTING` for tiling patterns and Type 3 glyphs (self-referencing content overflowed the stack); (7) CID width ranges in `/W` and `/W2` clamped to `MAX_CID` (a `0 4294967295 w` range hung); (8) `InterpreterSettings::hide_comments` skips markup annotations but keeps widgets and links (View ▸ Hide all comments); (9) `image_size_ok`: images and masks over 2^28 pixels are not decoded (a fuzzed `/W 4294967295` stencil mask allocated 4 GiB); (10) `MAX_NESTED_PAINTS`: nested paints (forms, Type 3 glyphs and tiling patterns inside one another) share a per-page budget of 50,000 (a glyph showing eight glyphs of its own font, sixteen deep, hung); (11) depends on skrifa 0.47 instead of 0.42 (upstream read-fonts fixed a Type 1 tokenizer that recursed through runs of numbers: a fuzzed font hung or overflowed the stack), with the one API change (`Charset::glyph_id` returns `Option`); (12) annotation appearances whose `/BBox` or `/Matrix` collapses to a line or a point are skipped (mapping them onto `/Rect` divided by zero and handed the device infinite or NaN matrices); (13) a Highlight annotation without a usable normal appearance is drawn from its `/QuadPoints`, `/C` and `/CA` with Multiply blending, as pdfcraft-annot draws highlights (it was not drawn at all); (14) simple-font `/Widths` (`read_widths`): entries only for codes 0–255 (one entry per code below `/FirstChar` was allocated: `4294967295` asked for 34 GB), an entry that isn't a number leaves its code missing instead of ending the array, and a `/LastChar` below `/FirstChar` gives no widths instead of discarding the font for a standard one; (15) the appearance box is mapped onto `/Rect` corner to corner: the translation now accounts for the scale (an appearance whose box didn't start at the origin and differed in size from `/Rect` was drawn shifted); (16) a clip set by `W`/`W*` takes effect after whichever path-painting operator ends the path (`S`, `f`, `B`, … as well as `n`; ISO 32000-2 §8.5.4): it was applied only on `n`, so `re W* S` clipped nothing and the clip stayed pending for a later, unrelated `n` | (1) `raster::tests::widget_appearance_states`; (2, 3) `xtask text-oracle` on corpus/pdfjs issue918; (4) `raster::tests::layer_override_hides_content`; (5) `raster::tests::soft_mask_without_group_colour_space_is_applied`; (6) `raster::tests::self_referencing_tiling_pattern_terminates`, `raster::tests::self_referencing_type3_glyph_terminates`; (7) `raster::tests::huge_cid_width_ranges_terminate`; (8) `raster::tests::hiding_comments_keeps_fields`; (9) `raster::tests::absurd_mask_and_fax_sizes_are_refused_before_decoding`; (10) `raster::tests::type3_glyphs_that_fan_out_into_themselves_finish`; (11) `raster::tests::type1_font_programs_with_long_runs_of_numbers_load_quickly`; (12) `raster::tests::degenerate_annotation_appearances_are_skipped`; (13) `raster::tests::highlights_without_an_appearance_are_drawn`; (14) `raster::tests::malformed_simple_font_widths_keep_later_widths_and_the_font`, `raster::tests::huge_simple_font_first_char_terminates`; (15) `raster::tests::annotation_appearance_box_maps_onto_rect`; (16) `raster::tests::clipping_path_applies_after_any_painting_operator` |

| hayro | 0.7.1 | Apache-2.0 OR MIT | (1) `RenderSettings::{x_offset, y_offset}` to render one tile of a large page; (2) images over `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` (2^28) are skipped (a fuzzed `/W 4294967295` hung in resampling); (3) `tiling_cell_scale` keeps a tiling pattern's cell pixmap within 3000 px a side whatever its `/XStep`/`/YStep` (a fuzzed step far beyond `/BBox` allocated 2 GB); (4) stroke widths clamped to 4 × (canvas width + height) device pixels (a fuzzed `/LW 9223372036854775807` allocated 10 GB in stroke expansion) | (1) `raster::tests::tiles_match_full_render`; (2) `raster::tests::absurd_image_dimensions_are_skipped`; (3) `raster::tests::tiling_cells_stay_small_whatever_the_step`; (4) `raster::tests::absurd_predictor_columns_and_line_widths_render` |
| hayro-jbig2 | 0.3.0 | Apache-2.0 OR MIT | (1) at most 2^28 pixels per bitmap, page bitmap, halftone grid and grayscale image (each side could be 65535: 4.3 billion pixels decoded one by one); (2) at most 2^26 symbol pixels per symbol dictionary (a fuzzed dictionary decoded for minutes) | (1) `raster::tests::jbig2_regions_of_billions_of_pixels_are_refused`; (2) the nightly `cargo xtask fuzz` finding, which now finishes in about a second |
| lopdf | 0.45.0 | MIT | (1) PNG predictor rows longer than the data are refused before their buffers are allocated (a fuzzed `/Columns 4294967295` allocated two 4 GiB rows); (2) predictor row widths use saturating arithmetic | (1) `inspect::tests::png_predictor_rows_longer_than_the_data_are_refused_before_allocating` |
| hayro-syntax | 0.7.2 | Apache-2.0 OR MIT | (1) Page-tree cycle guard in `resolve_pages` (visited set + depth cap): a `/Kids` loop among compressed objects overflowed the stack and aborted the process; (2) `ccitt_size_ok`: CCITT images wider than 2^20 columns or over 2^28 pixels are not decoded (a fuzzed `/Columns 4294967295` allocated 4 GiB); (3) Flate/LZW predictor row widths are saturating `usize`, a zero width is refused and a row longer than the data is not allocated (a fuzzed `/Columns 9223372036854775807` wrapped to a 2^61-byte allocation and aborted); (4) the inline-image end-of-data check (`EI`) doesn't nest inside its own look-ahead and examines at most 256 candidates and steps (50 images with "EI" in their data ran for over ten minutes); (5) a stream whose `/Length` is wrong is recovered only when `stream` is the next token — scanning ahead to a later object's `stream` made an indirect appearance-state dictionary (Quartz checkboxes: `/AP /N` → `<< /Yes … /Off … >>`) render as a non-form, so the widget was skipped | (1) `cos/tests/writer.rs::page_tree_loops_in_object_streams_do_not_crash_readers`; (2) `raster::tests::absurd_mask_and_fax_sizes_are_refused_before_decoding`; (3) `raster::tests::absurd_predictor_columns_and_line_widths_render`; (4) `raster::tests::inline_images_with_ei_in_their_data_parse_in_linear_time`; (5) `raster::tests::indirect_appearance_state_dict_is_not_another_stream` |

Temporary: hayro is the bootstrap renderer and lopdf the bootstrap inspector (ADR-0004); M2.6 replaces them with our own devices and `cos`/`model`.

Text extraction: hayro-interpret exposes `OutlineGlyph::is_vertical` from a Type0 font’s CMap writing mode. PdfCraft follows negative glyph-space y for WMode 1 so upright vertical columns can be searched (#126).

Embed build patches (marked `Embed build:` in the source; used by the save inspector, `pdfcraft-engine` `inspect`):

| Crate | Patch | Why | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| hayro | `render_upright`: render a page as if its `/Rotate` were 0 (`render`'s body moved into `render_with`, which takes the page transform and size) | Comparing a page with an earlier version whose rotation differs; un-rotating the pixels of a rotated render is not pixel-identical to an upright render | `pdfcraft-render` `content::tests::renders_a_rotated_page_upright`, `pdfcraft-engine` `inspect::tests::a_page_rotated_and_redacted_in_one_save_is_compared_upright` |
| hayro-syntax | `XRef::is_repaired` made public | hayro rebuilds a broken cross-reference table silently, on opening or on the first object it cannot find; what it then reads may differ from what other readers read, so the inspector refuses such a file | `pdfcraft-render` `content::tests::says_when_the_cross_reference_data_was_rebuilt` |
| hayro-interpret | A work counter: `InterpreterSettings::work_budget` (unbounded by default), charged one unit per operator, four per glyph, and three per fill, stroke, image or shading plus one per 256 device pixels it covers inside the clip; past the budget the rest of the interpretation is skipped and `InterpreterWarning::WorkBudgetExceeded` is sent once; `work_spent()` reads the latest interpretation's total (thread-local, reset by `Context::new` as the nested-paint budget is) | Rendering time grows with paints × area, not with content bytes: a page of cheap-to-parse fills can take seconds, and wasm32 has no clock to stop it. The counter bounds every interpretation on every target | `pdfcraft-render` `content::tests::stops_an_interpretation_at_its_work_budget`, `pdfcraft-engine` `inspect::tests::pages_of_millions_of_operations_stop_on_the_work_budget_not_the_clock` |
| hayro-interpret | Paint-time work: the budget, its warning sink and a per-interpretation byte count are thread-local (set by `Context::new`), so devices charge what they compute: `spend_work(units)`, `spend_allocation(bytes)` (an interpretation's buffers may total `MAX_ALLOCATION`, 256 MiB; past it, refused before allocating). `Function::cost` / `ShadingFunction::cost` (operators per evaluation; a PostScript calculator its operator count). `ShadingPattern::encode_within(area)` samples meshes only inside the texture's area (a triangle far larger than the page was walked whole: 2 GB from a 1 KB file), charging triangles, pixels walked and the sample map before building them (at most 500,000 triangles; a patch is 722). Image decodes are charged by pixel count and their buffer | A shading, mesh or tiling cell costs pixels × function work, not the clipped area the interpreter sees (one page took 72 s at 1 % of the budget) | `pdfcraft-engine` `inspect::tests::costly_shadings_tilings_and_meshes_stop_on_the_work_budget` |
| hayro | `set_paint` charges a shading texture (its pixels × (1 + function cost / 32) / 8 units, and its buffer) and a tiling cell (its pixels / 256, and its buffer) before computing it, painting nothing once refused; a soft mask is charged by its canvas area | As above | As above |
| hayro-syntax | `budget`: a per-thread bound on stream decoding, unbounded unless set (`set_decode_budget`, `decode_spent`, `decode_budget_exceeded`). Every filter's output is charged (`Stream::decoded_image`); Flate (both decoders), LZW and RunLength stop as soon as their output would pass what is left; DCT, JPX and CCITT check the samples their header declares (and JBIG2 its page size) before decoding, as codec work weighed per codec (DCT and CCITT one a sample, JPX four, JBIG2 four a pixel made or composed) | The interpreter's work counter saw neither decoded bytes nor codec work: a compressed stream could expand without limit, and a codec's own size (larger than the image dictionary's `/Width` × `/Height`, which is what was charged) was decoded and converted whole | `pdfcraft-render` `content::tests::decoding_stops_at_the_decode_budget` |
| hayro-jbig2 | `budget`: a per-thread allowance of pixels, charged when a bitmap is made or re-sized and when one is composed onto another; past it bitmaps are refused, compositions skipped and `work_exceeded` set (`set_work_allowance`, `work_spent`); unbounded unless set | A text or halftone region composes up to 10,000 symbols or a grid of patterns, each up to 2^26 pixels: the existing pixel caps bound memory, not work | Not covered by a test with JBIG2 data (see the fix round 4 report); unbounded behaviour is unchanged by construction (`spend` returns true without an allowance) |
| hayro-interpret | `Context::new` sets the decode budget for each interpretation with a work budget (`MAX_DECODED` 256 MiB, `MAX_CODEC_WORK` 2^27) and clears it otherwise; parsing a font program costs one unit per 64 bytes; glyphs are not hinted under a budget (hinting runs the font's programs); a glyph outline costs 16 units and one per eight elements when loaded, and has at most `MAX_OUTLINE_ELEMENTS` (65,536) elements under a budget (past it the outline is empty and the budget spent); an image whose codec size exceeds its dictionary's is charged the difference after decoding | Font programs, outlines and codec-sized images were unmetered (fix round 3 review, unmeasured items; Ruling R6b-16) | `pdfcraft-render` `content::tests::an_embedded_font_program_and_its_outlines_are_work`, `decoding_stops_at_the_decode_budget` |
| hayro | Drawing a glyph costs its cached outline's elements (one unit per eight); a soft mask charges its buffers (ten bytes a canvas pixel) and its area before it is made, and once refused is left empty instead of being drawn (its charge's result was ignored) | As above; the soft-mask charge was `let _ =` (fix round 3 review) | `pdfcraft-render` `content::tests::a_soft_mask_past_the_budget_is_too_complex` |
| hayro-interpret | `StencilImage::stream` and `StencilImage::paint` (a stencil mask's stream and fill, as `RasterImage::stream` gives a raster image's, without decoding it); `SoftMask::use_key` (which setting of a soft mask a value is: each `gs` makes a new one, restoring a state hands back the same) | The save inspector takes image placements from the interpretation that renders the page (Ruling R6b-18): its device must name every image it is handed, stencils included, and interpret each soft mask's group once per setting for the images drawn there | `pdfcraft-engine` `inspect::placement_tests::a_stencil_mask_is_placed_like_any_image`, `image_placements_are_where_the_interpreter_draws` (the soft mask case) |
| hayro-syntax | `resolved`: a per-thread log, open only when asked (`open_log`, `close_log`), of every object read through the cross-reference data with where it was read (file offset, or object stream and index) and of every file stream's data range, recorded in `XRef::get_with` and `Stream::read` | The save inspector reads structure with `pdfcraft_cos` and pixels and text with hayro; a file the two resolve differently (another object for a reference, another stream extent) would let the facts describe two documents, so the inspector checks every object hayro read against `pdfcraft_cos` | `pdfcraft-engine` `inspect::agreement_tests` |
| hayro-syntax | The content iterators record where their reading stops: `UntypedIter::next`'s body moved, unchanged, into `advance`, and `next` records (`resolved::content_stopped`) a reading that ends with more than white space and comments left, as does a failed operator read; `TypedIter::next` records a path operator it rejects (its operator list moved into `PATH_OPERATORS`) unless only white space and comments follow, through `Instruction::stops_if_rejected`; the end-of-data heuristic's look-ahead records nothing. The `resolved` log also counts these stops (`stopped`) and keeps the decoded data of each content stream interpreted besides a page's own (`content`; another decoding of the same object, or a content stream without an object number, is a conflict) | Content hayro stops reading before its end is checked by nothing (its text, images and render all end there), though another viewer may read on; the save inspector refuses it (Ruling R6b-20). The decoded data lets the inspector check that `pdfcraft_cos` decodes every content stream hayro interprets to the same bytes, so content streams can be compared by their decoded data | `pdfcraft-engine` `inspect::conformance_tests::content_after_an_operator_that_ends_the_reading_is_refused`, `a_base_whose_content_stops_early_is_the_base_s_problem` |
| hayro-interpret | `Device::draw_form` (provided, doing nothing): called before a form XObject's content is interpreted, with the form's object and its `/BBox` in device space. Forms, tiling patterns' cells and Type 3 glyph procedures log their decoded content (`resolved::content`); one whose data cannot be decoded is logged as a content stream not read (`resolved::content_stopped`) instead of being skipped silently | The save inspector compares forms by their decoded content in a rewrite and must know where each was drawn (a changed form must lie wholly under the redaction boxes), and refuses a page whose content hayro did not wholly read (Ruling R6b-20) | `pdfcraft-engine` `inspect::conformance_tests` (forms, Type 3 glyph procedures, stops in forms and glyph procedures) |
| hayro-interpret | `InterpreterSettings::all_layers_visible` (`false` by default): every optional-content layer is interpreted as visible (`OcgState::all_visible`, set by `Context::new_with`); marked content is still tracked, but `is_visible` answers true, so no `BDC`, `/OC` entry, configuration or `ocg_overrides` hides anything | The save inspector compares a page's text, images and pixels in every layer (Ruling R6b-23): which layers show is each viewer's choice (a Layers panel shows hidden ones), and hayro hid content other readers show (any `BDC` naming a group, a group listed in `/OFF` but not in `/OCGs`, a membership dictionary's `/VE` ignored) | `pdfcraft-engine` `inspect::conformance_tests::text_added_where_hayro_alone_hid_it_is_seen`, `text_added_in_a_layer_that_is_off_is_a_change_outside_redactions`, `an_image_in_optional_content_that_is_off_is_drawn_and_compared` |
| hayro-interpret | Optional-content marks (`ocg.rs`, `interpret/mod.rs`, `x_object.rs`, `context.rs`): drawing every layer, each level of marked content opened is recorded per thread with what hayro took for optional content (`LayerMark`: the `BDC` tag, the object of the named property list, of an inline list's `/OC` or of an XObject's `/OC`; any `/OC`-tagged `BDC` and any XObject `/OC` hayro cannot take for a dictionary are recorded too); `current_layers()` gives the marks open now (one `Arc` until one opens or closes), `layers_report()` every mark met since `Context::new` and whether marked content was unbalanced (an `EMC` closing what its content stream did not open, a form's content leaving a level open, a level open at the end of an interpretation). `InterpreterSettings::hidden_layers` (empty by default): with `all_layers_visible`, a level naming one of these objects hides what is inside it. `OcgState::begin_*` take the mark; with `all_layers_visible` off nothing is recorded and visibility is computed as before | The save inspector makes each glyph's, image's and form's optional-content membership and default visibility part of its identity, evaluated by the inspector itself against `/OCProperties` (hayro ignores `/VE`, hides groups named by other tags, …), refuses what it cannot evaluate, and renders the page at its default view and with every layer off (Ruling R6b-29) | `pdfcraft-engine` `inspect::layer_tests` |
| hayro-interpret | `Glyph::identity`: a glyph's font dictionary's object and its glyph ID (a Type 3 glyph's code); `Font` keeps the object (third field) and `OutlineGlyph`/`Type3Glyph` carry it (`font_object`). `Context::resolve_font` gives it only when the dictionary is its object's whole data: a dictionary written directly inside another object reports that object's number | The save inspector names a glyph without a Unicode value by its font and glyph instead of refusing the page (Ruling R6b-25 (c)); a direct font dictionary has no object of its own, so its glyphs are still refused | `pdfcraft-engine` `inspect::tests::glyphs_without_text_are_named_by_their_font_and_glyph`, `inspect::glyphs::tests::glyphs_without_text_pair_by_font_and_glyph` |
